name: Matt glazing
summary: A thick, dry-looking glaze with a velvet surface. The potter adds alumina or a silica surplus, so that fine crystals make the surface dull.
how: Add alumina or a surplus of silica to the glaze, so that it does not melt to glass.
Apply the glaze thick, 1 to 2 mm, by dipping or by brush.
Fire it to the full heat and cool it slowly.
Wipe the shoulder clean of drips to show the form.

origin.note: The Grueby Faience Company sells vases with a thick matt green glaze and moulded leaves.

adoptions.via: Grueby and then Rookwood, Newcomb and others sell vases in a velvet matt glaze, with leaf and flower reliefs.
The Steubenville Pottery sprays soft matt and satin glazes in grey, sea green and cinnamon on American Modern.
